# Phlix

> Phlix (App Store name "Phlix Photos") is an independent iPhone and iPad app that works with Plex Media Server. It shows the photos and videos in your Plex photo libraries by folder or on a date timeline with a year scrubber, saves them to the Photos app or straight into an album, and plays slideshows. With Screen Mirroring on, or over an HDMI adapter, the TV shows just the photos while your iPhone shows the controls (Phlix Pro; without Pro, the TV mirrors the phone). From version 1.0.21, Camera Upload (Beta) backs up the photos and videos on an iPhone or iPad to the user's own Plex photo library, on the home Wi-Fi only. Phlix is not made by Plex.

Phlix is an independent application and is not affiliated with, endorsed, or sponsored by Plex, Inc.
Plex, the Plex Play logo, and Plex Media Server are trademarks of Plex GmbH and used under a license.

This is the long version of https://phlixapp.com/llms.txt: the same facts, then the full text of the key English pages.

## Answers

### What happened to Plex Camera Upload?
Plex announced on its forum on March 18, 2021 that it was ending support for Camera Upload in its apps, with removal targeted for June 2021; photos already uploaded stayed in Plex. Source: Plex's announcement "Important info about Camera Upload in Plex" (archived copy, the original page is no longer online): https://web.archive.org/web/20210319005631/https://forums.plex.tv/t/important-info-about-camera-upload-in-plex/700626 . In August 2025 a moderator on Plex's forum wrote that the feature "was discontinued about 4 years ago": https://forums.plex.tv/t/plex-photos-app-not-uploading-to-server/927683 . Full answer: https://phlixapp.com/plex-camera-upload/

### How do I back up iPhone photos to Plex?
Plex shows the photos that are in a folder of a Plex photo library, after it scans. So phone photos must be copied into such a folder. To do that automatically, use Camera Upload (Beta) in Phlix: install the free Phlix Camera Upload helper (one Docker container) on the machine that runs Plex Media Server, pointed at a folder inside the Plex photo library, then turn on Settings > Camera Upload in Phlix. It uploads only on the home Wi-Fi, never over mobile data, to the user's own server only, as a one-way copy that never deletes anything on the phone. The first 100 uploads are free; Phlix Pro uploads the rest. It needs Phlix 1.0.21 or later. If the App Store does not offer that version yet, it is on its way. Setup guide: https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/ . By hand, without an app: copy the photos into that folder (for example from the iPhone's Files app connected to a shared folder on the server, or from a computer), then let Plex scan.

### Is there an alternative to the Plex Photos app?
Plex Photos is Plex's own free app for photo libraries; its App Store page lists Recommended View, Timeline View and Library View, and its latest version is 2025.2.0 (June 12, 2025). Phlix is an independent alternative for iPhone and iPad that works with the same Plex Media Server: folders and a date timeline with a year scrubber, slideshows that include subfolders, saves to Photos or an album, big-screen slideshows on the TV, and Camera Upload (Beta). It is free to browse. Full answer: https://phlixapp.com/plex-photos-alternative/

## Facts

- Website: https://phlixapp.com
- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/phlix-photos/id6796820208 (App ID 6796820208)
- Developer: Jason Loomis (independent developer)
- Platforms: iPhone and iPad, iOS and iPadOS 17 or later. A Mac with Apple silicon (macOS 14 or later) can install the iPad version; Apple lists it as designed for iPad, not verified for macOS.
- Category: Photo & Video
- Current App Store version: 1.0.20. Camera Upload (Beta) comes with version 1.0.21. If the App Store does not offer that version yet, it is on its way.
- Languages: English, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese (Brazil), Dutch, Swedish, Danish, Norwegian Bokmål, Finnish, Polish, Japanese, Korean, Chinese (Simplified and Traditional)
- Needs: a Plex Media Server with at least one photo library, and a Plex account. No Plex Pass on the home network. For video, Plex requires a Plex Pass (the server owner's or the user's own) or a Remote Watch Pass to stream remotely; Plex says photos stream remotely for free (https://support.plex.tv/articles/requirements-for-remote-playback-of-personal-media/). Some servers send only smaller copies of photos over the internet, so away from home a photo or a save can be a converted copy.

## Features

- Folders that follow the folders on the server, and a date timeline one tap away, with a year scrubber: tap 1987 to see just that year
- Built for big libraries: loads a page at a time instead of everything at once (libraries of 100,000+ photos)
- Full-screen viewer with pinch to zoom, and a video player that remembers where you stopped
- Slideshows of a folder, a year or the whole library; a folder's slideshow also plays the folders inside it (switch: Include Subfolders); 2, 4, 6 or 10 seconds a slide, shuffle, loop, hard cuts between photos
- Big-screen slideshows (Pro): with Screen Mirroring on, or over an HDMI adapter, the TV shows just the photos while your iPhone shows the controls. Without Pro, the TV mirrors the phone.
- Save to Photos: 25 free saves, unlimited with Pro. The original file when the server sends it; otherwise a copy the server converted, which may be smaller.
- Save to Album: pick an album once (Settings > Storage > Save to Album, or ••• on a photo > Save to Album…) and every save goes into it
- Camera Upload (Beta, from version 1.0.21): backs up the device's photos and videos to a folder of the user's Plex photo library through a free helper next to Plex Media Server; home Wi-Fi only; encrypted (HTTPS, pinned certificate); the Plex server's owner pairs without a code, others with the helper's pairing code; first 100 uploads free
- Search photo and video titles, tags and collections; favorites saved on the device
- Your own server or one shared with you; switch between its photo libraries
- On cellular and in Low Data Mode, Phlix stops loading ahead
- iPad sidebar with your libraries; VoiceOver support
- Sign-in on Plex's own sign-in page: Phlix never sees the password, and there is no Phlix account
- Phlix never changes or deletes what is on the server; Camera Upload only adds new files, in the folder chosen for it

## Pricing

- Free: browsing, timeline, year scrubber, search, favorites, on-device slideshows, 25 saves to Photos, and the first 100 camera uploads (Beta, from version 1.0.21)
- Pro Lifetime: $19.99 once, with Family Sharing. Unlimited saves, big-screen slideshows, unlimited camera uploads (Beta)
- Pro Yearly: $6.99 a year, renews until cancelled. Same Pro features
- 14-day trial of Pro: not a subscription, never renews, never charges

## Privacy

- No ads, no tracking pixels, no session replay, no third-party advertising SDKs
- Anonymous usage, error and crash statistics tied to a random ID on the device, never the user's name, Plex account, photos, file names or server address; can be turned off in Settings
- Camera Upload sends photos only to the helper on the user's own server, never to the developer
- Privacy policy: https://phlixapp.com/privacy/

# Full text of the key pages

The sections below are the text of these English pages of phlixapp.com, as of November 24, 2026.

## Homepage: frequently asked questions (https://phlixapp.com/#faq)

### Frequently Asked Questions

#### What is Phlix?

Phlix is an independent iPhone and iPad app that works with Plex Media Server. It shows the photos and videos in your Plex photo libraries by folder or on a date timeline with a year scrubber, saves photos to the Photos app or straight into an album, and plays slideshows of a folder, a year or the whole library. With Screen Mirroring on, or over an HDMI adapter, the TV shows just the photos while your iPhone shows the controls (Phlix Pro; without Pro, the TV mirrors the phone). From version 1.0.21, Camera Upload (Beta) backs up your camera roll to your own server.

#### What happened to Plex's Camera Upload?

Plex announced on its forum on March 18, 2021 that it was ending support for Camera Upload, with removal targeted for June 2021. Photos that were already uploaded stayed in Plex. Phlix, an independent app, has its own Camera Upload (Beta) from version 1.0.21: it copies the photos and videos on your iPhone or iPad into a folder of your Plex photo library, on your home Wi-Fi, through a free helper you run next to Plex Media Server. The whole story, with Plex's announcement (https://phlixapp.com/plex-camera-upload/).

#### How do I back up my iPhone photos to Plex?

Put them in a folder that one of your Plex photo libraries includes, and let Plex scan it. Camera Upload (Beta) in Phlix does that for you: install the free Phlix Camera Upload helper, one Docker container, on the machine that runs Plex Media Server, then turn it on in Phlix under Settings › Camera Upload. At home, on your Wi-Fi, it backs up new photos by itself. The first 100 uploads are free, and Phlix Pro uploads the rest. It needs Phlix 1.0.21 or later. If the App Store does not offer that version yet, it is on its way. The setup guide (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/) has every step.

#### Is there an alternative to the Plex Photos app?

Plex Photos is Plex's own free app for photo libraries. Phlix is an independent alternative for iPhone and iPad that works with the same Plex Media Server: folders and a date timeline with a year scrubber, slideshows that include subfolders, saves to Photos or into an album, big-screen slideshows on your TV, and Camera Upload (Beta). Phlix is free to browse, so you can try it on your own library. Phlix as a Plex Photos alternative (https://phlixapp.com/plex-photos-alternative/).

#### Do I need Plex Pass to use Phlix?

No Plex Pass is needed on your home network. Away from home, Plex requires a Plex Pass (the server owner's or your own) or a Remote Watch Pass on your account to stream personal video remotely; Plex says music and photos stream remotely for free (Plex: Requirements for Remote Playback of Personal Media (https://support.plex.tv/articles/requirements-for-remote-playback-of-personal-media/)). Phlix itself needs only a Plex account and a Plex Media Server with at least one photo library. Camera Upload needs no Plex Pass either.

#### How much does Phlix cost?

Phlix is free to download. Browsing, the timeline, search, favorites and on-device slideshows are free forever, with 25 saves to Photos and, from version 1.0.21, the first 100 camera uploads. Phlix Pro removes those limits and adds big-screen slideshows on your TV: $19.99 once, with Family Sharing, or $6.99 a year. You can try Pro free for 14 days; the trial never renews and never charges you.

#### Can I save photos from Plex into an album on my iPhone?

Yes. Pick an album once, and every photo you save from Phlix goes straight into it: Settings › Storage › Save to Album, or tap ••• on any photo and choose Save to Album. Pick one of your albums, or make a new one. Choosing an album asks iOS for full access to Photos, because albums need it. If you don't choose one, saves go to your library as before.

#### How many photos can Phlix handle?

Phlix is built for big libraries: it loads a page at a time instead of everything at once. Server-side year filtering, virtual paging and prefetching handle libraries of 100,000+ photos. The first screen appears in seconds; the year index fills in behind it.

#### How does the AirPlay slideshow work?

With Screen Mirroring on, or over an HDMI adapter, the TV shows just the photos while your iPhone shows the controls. Phlix draws its own full-screen window on the TV and asks your server for an image sized to the display, with hard cuts between photos. Choose 2, 4, 6 or 10 seconds a slide, shuffle and loop. This is a Phlix Pro feature; without Pro, the TV mirrors your iPhone's screen.

#### Which languages does Phlix speak?

English, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese (Brazil), Dutch, Swedish, Danish, Norwegian, Finnish, Polish, Japanese, Korean, and Chinese, Simplified and Traditional. Phlix follows the language your iPhone or iPad is set to.

#### Does Phlix work on iPad and Mac?

Phlix is one app for iPhone and iPad; on iPad, a sidebar lists your libraries. On a Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or later, macOS 14 or later), the App Store offers the iPad version. Apple lists it as designed for iPad and not verified for macOS.

#### Is my data private with Phlix?

Yes. Phlix has no ads, no tracking pixels and no session replay. It sends anonymous usage, error and crash statistics tied to a random ID on your device, never your name, Plex account, photos, file names or server address, and you can turn that off in Settings. Camera Upload sends your photos only to the helper on your own server. See the Privacy Policy (https://phlixapp.com/privacy/) for full details.

#### What makes Phlix different from Plex Photos?

Plex Photos is Plex's own app; its App Store page lists a recommended view, a timeline view and a library view. Phlix is an independent app with folders that follow your server, a date timeline with a year scrubber, slideshows of a folder (with the folders inside it), a year or the whole library, saves to Photos or into an album, big-screen slideshows with Screen Mirroring or an HDMI adapter, a cellular data saver and, from version 1.0.21, Camera Upload (Beta).

#### Can I use Phlix outside my home network?

Yes, for browsing, as long as your Plex server allows remote access. Phlix connects to whichever server address is reachable, local or remote. For video, Plex requires a Plex Pass (the server owner's or your own) or a Remote Watch Pass to stream remotely; Plex says photos stream remotely for free (Plex: Requirements for Remote Playback of Personal Media (https://support.plex.tv/articles/requirements-for-remote-playback-of-personal-media/)). Some servers send only smaller copies of photos over the internet, so away from home a photo or a save can be a converted copy. Camera Upload is different on purpose: it uploads only on your home Wi-Fi.

#### Does the lifetime purchase include Family Sharing?

Yes. The $19.99 Pro Lifetime purchase is Family Shareable through Apple Family Sharing. Buy once and your whole family can use Pro on their devices.

#### What happens after the 14-day trial?

After 14 days, Phlix returns to the free tier: saves beyond your 25 free ones, camera uploads beyond your 100 free ones and big-screen slideshows need Pro again. You keep full access to browsing, the timeline, search, favorites and on-device slideshows. Nothing is deleted and nothing is charged. You can upgrade to Pro anytime.

#### Is Phlix made by Plex?

No. Phlix is an independent application and is not affiliated with, endorsed, or sponsored by Plex, Inc. It connects to your Plex Media Server using publicly available APIs.

## Plex Camera Upload: what happened, and what to use now (https://phlixapp.com/plex-camera-upload/)

Photos · Answers

Updated November 24, 2026 · 5 min read

### The short answer

Plex's own Camera Upload is gone. Plex announced on its forum in March 2021 that it was ending the feature, with removal targeted for June 2021.

To get the photos on your iPhone or iPad into Plex now, they have to land in a folder that one of your Plex photo libraries includes. Plex then scans them in like any other photo.

To do that automatically, use Camera Upload (Beta) in Phlix, an independent app that works with Plex Media Server. It copies your camera roll to a free helper that runs next to Plex Media Server, on your home Wi-Fi only, and the photos show up in your Plex photo library.

Camera Upload (Beta) needs Phlix 1.0.21 or later. If the App Store does not offer that version yet, it is on its way.

### What happened to Plex's Camera Upload?

Plex added Camera Upload to its mobile apps in 2014. It copied the photos on a phone to the owner's Plex Media Server. In March 2021, Plex posted Important info about Camera Upload in Plex in the Announcements section of its forum:

“Today we are ending support for the Camera Upload feature for those who do not have it enabled. Existing users that have it enabled may continue to use it as-is for now, but it will be removed in a future version of Plex. The current target for removal is 90 days from now (estimated June 2021).” The Plex Team, Plex Forum, Announcements, March 18, 2021 (archived copy (https://web.archive.org/web/20210319005631/https://forums.plex.tv/t/important-info-about-camera-upload-in-plex/700626); the original forum page is no longer online)

The same announcement said that photos already added through Camera Upload would not be affected, and gave Plex's reasons: many other apps now offered camera upload, and iOS and Android had brought “new formats, background processing APIs, and privacy restrictions on how apps like Plex are allowed to access users’ photos.”

The feature did not come back. In August 2025, when someone on Plex's forum asked whether the new Plex Photos app could upload the photos on their phone, a forum moderator answered: “That feature was discontinued about 4 years ago.” (Plex Forum, August 1, 2025 (https://forums.plex.tv/t/plex-photos-app-not-uploading-to-server/927683))

### How to get iPhone photos into Plex now

Plex shows the photos that are inside the folders of a Plex photo library, once it has scanned them. So every way of getting phone photos into Plex comes down to one thing: putting the files into such a folder. There are two ways to do that.

#### 1. Automatically, at home: Camera Upload (Beta) in Phlix

Camera Upload in Phlix backs up the photos and videos on your iPhone or iPad to the server in your home, while the device is on your home Wi-Fi. It has two parts. The Phlix app on the phone reads your camera roll. A small free program on your server, the Camera Upload helper, receives the photos and writes them into a folder of your Plex photo library. The helper is one Docker container, and its source code is public.
- Only at home. Phlix uploads on your home Wi-Fi and nowhere else. Never over mobile data.
- Only to you. Photos go from your phone straight to your server, encrypted. None of them go to Phlix or to a cloud service.
- Only copies. Nothing is ever deleted or changed on your phone.
- In your Plex library. Each device gets its own folder, with a folder for each year and month, so the photos show up in Plex, and in Phlix, next to everything else.

The helper is free. In the app, the first 100 uploads are free, and Phlix Pro (https://phlixapp.com/#pricing) uploads the rest. Camera Upload is a beta: keep your own backup of anything you cannot replace. What the beta does, and what it does not do (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#beta).

#### 2. By hand, now and then

Without an app, copy the photos yourself, then let Plex scan:
- From the iPhone. In the Files app, connect to a shared folder on your server (Browse, then the ••• button, then Connect to Server). Then in the Photos app, select the photos, tap Share, and choose Save to Files with that folder.
- From a computer. Import the photos from the iPhone to the computer, then copy them into the folder of your Plex photo library.
- Then, in Plex, scan the photo library, or switch on Settings › Library › Scan my library automatically so that Plex picks up new files by itself. That setting depends on the server noticing new files, which typically fails for folders mounted over the network; then also switch on Scan my library periodically (Plex: Library settings (https://support.plex.tv/articles/200289526-library/)).

That works, and it needs nothing new on your server. It is also easy to forget, which is what Camera Upload is for.

### Camera Upload (Beta) in three steps

#### Install the helper

One Docker container on the machine that runs Plex Media Server, pointed at a folder inside your Plex photo library.

#### Connect your iPhone

In Phlix, open Settings › Camera Upload. Phlix finds the helper on your network and pairs with it.

#### At home

On your home Wi-Fi, new photos copy to your server: straight away while Phlix is open, and in short bursts while it is closed.

On a Linux computer or server, or a Mac with Docker Desktop, step 1 is one command in a terminal on the server. The installer checks Docker, asks for your upload folder and starts the helper:

```
curl -fsSL https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/install.sh | sh
```

On Windows, Unraid, Synology, TrueNAS SCALE and QNAP, or to let an AI assistant do it, follow the setup guide's Step 1 (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#install). Then, in Phlix, tap Check for the Helper, then Check My Network. Nothing is switched on, and nothing is uploaded, until the helper is found. When Phlix says Helper found, name this device's folder and tap Connect. The owner of the Plex server pairs without a code; family members type the helper's pairing code. All the steps, with screenshots (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#connect).

### Where the photos go

Each phone or tablet gets its own folder inside the upload folder, with one folder for each year and one for each month:

```
Camera Uploads/
  Anna's iPhone/
    2026/
      2026-11/
        IMG_1234.HEIC
        IMG_1235.MOV
```

A file keeps its name and its date. The same photo from two phones is stored once, and nothing is ever overwritten. When your Plex account owns the server, Phlix asks Plex to scan once your photos have arrived. To be sure, switch on Scan my library automatically in Plex as well.

### Questions

#### Does Plex still have Camera Upload?

Plex announced on its forum on March 18, 2021 that it was ending support for Camera Upload, with removal targeted for June 2021. In August 2025, a moderator on Plex's forum described the feature as discontinued about four years earlier. Photos uploaded before that stayed in Plex.

#### How do I back up my iPhone photos to Plex automatically?

Camera Upload (Beta) in Phlix does it. Install the free Phlix Camera Upload helper, one Docker container, on the machine that runs Plex Media Server, and point it at a folder inside your Plex photo library. Then turn on Settings > Camera Upload in Phlix. At home, on your Wi-Fi, new photos copy to your server by themselves. It needs Phlix 1.0.21 or later. If the App Store does not offer that version yet, it is on its way.

#### Can I put iPhone photos into Plex without an app?

Yes, by hand. Copy the photos into a folder that one of your Plex photo libraries includes, then let Plex scan the library. From an iPhone, the Files app can connect to a shared folder on your server, and in the Photos app, Share > Save to Files copies the selected photos there. From a computer, import the photos from the iPhone and copy them into that folder.

#### Does Phlix Camera Upload need Plex Pass?

No. The helper writes ordinary files into a folder of your Plex photo library, which works with every Plex Media Server.

#### Does it upload away from home or over mobile data?

No, on purpose. Phlix uploads only while the iPhone or iPad is on your home Wi-Fi. Away from home it does not start uploads or look for your server, apart from rare cases that the privacy policy (https://phlixapp.com/privacy/#camera-upload) lists; even then, your photos go only to your own helper. Photos you take on a trip upload when you are back.

#### Does it delete photos from my iPhone?

No. It is a one-way copy. Phlix never deletes or changes anything in your Photo Library, and deleting a photo on the phone leaves the copy on the server.

#### What does it cost?

The helper is free, and its source code is public. In the app, the first 100 uploads are free, and Phlix Pro uploads the rest: $19.99 once, with Family Sharing, or $6.99 a year, with a 14-day free trial that never charges you.

#### What do I need?

Plex Media Server with a photo library, on a computer or NAS that runs Docker (Linux, a Mac or Windows PC with Docker Desktop, Synology, Unraid, TrueNAS SCALE or QNAP); Phlix 1.0.21 or later on an iPhone or iPad; and the phone and the server on the same home network.

#### Is Phlix made by Plex?

No. Phlix is an independent application and is not affiliated with, endorsed, or sponsored by Plex, Inc. It works with Plex Media Server.

#### Is there an Android version?

No. Phlix is an app for iPhone and iPad.
